subject: Admin activity logging scope, retention windows, and SFTP handshake for evidence delivery
messages:
From: Anna Cole <anna.cole@optimalabs.com>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: security@optimalabs.com
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: admin activity logging scope + export delivery preferences

Sergio — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Optima Labs is starting the SOC 2 readiness checklist and we need a clear picture of what admin and operator activity Redwood logs, how long those records are retained by default, and the options for us to pull an attested export. Specifically we need:

- Which event types are captured (admin web UI: role changes, permission grants, API keys created/rotated, model deploys, restart/scale ops, user session changes).
- Retention default for each bucket (short-term operational, medium-term audit, long-term legal hold).
- Redaction options for PII in logs (are identities pseudonymized in an export?).
- Supported export channels (S3 presigned, SFTP push, encrypted artifact via vendor portal).
- File formats, manifest/checksum approach, and a sample manifest we can include in our evidence package.

Our timeline: we need a scoping response by EOD Thursday so our compliance lead can slot Redwood into the evidence matrix. If you can attach a one-page export spec and a basic SFTP handshake template that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Anna Cole
Head of Security Programs
Optima Labs
(attachment: requirements_summary.pdf - listing Optima's evidence checks)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Cole <anna.cole@optimalabs.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity logging scope + export delivery preferences

Anna — appreciate the clear ask. Quick summary first, then I'm attaching a compact export spec and an SFTP handshake template for ops. High level answers below; see attached "admin_activity_export_spec.xlsx" for the mapping and sample manifest.

1) Event types logged (surface list):
- Admin Console: login attempts, MFA events, role changes, group membership changes, permission grants/revokes, service account creation
- Infrastructure ops: model deploys (version, runtime), replica scale up/down, restarts, hardware assignment, driver errors (operational metadata only)
- API-level admin events: API key create/delete/rotate, token scope changes, webhook config changes
- Data-access control events: dataset access grants, encryption key operations (KMS references)

2) Retention tiers (defaults):
- Operational (7 days full-fidelity) — high cardinality, used for realtime debugging and alerts
- Audit (90 days full-fidelity) — retained in compressed event store accessible for requests and exports
- Attested snapshot / evidence (rolling 3 years) — on-request snapshot bundles we sign and checksum; longer retention by agreement (legal hold)

3) Redaction/pseudonymization:
- Exports can be requested with identities hashed (SHA256 salt) or with full IDs. We do not redact action types (e.g., "role.grant") but can pseudonymize display names. See sheet "redaction_options" in the attachment.

4) Export channels and formats:
- S3 presigned PUT (recommended for large bundles)
- SFTP push (we initiate connection if customer provides endpoint and key)
- Secure HTTPS transfer to customer-managed endpoint with mutual TLS (mTLS)
- Formats: gzipped JSONL per-day with a top-level manifest.json containing checksums (sha256) and an index.csv for quick sampling

5) Manifest and checksum:
- Manifest includes: export_id, generation_time (RFC3339), file_list (file_name, sha256, uncompressed_size, record_count), schema_version, redaction_policy_applied, signer_certificate_id.

I'm attaching two files: admin_activity_export_spec.xlsx (maps event -> retention tier -> example export row) and sftp_handshake_instructions.txt (includes key exchange steps and sample known_hosts entry).

Next steps: Kim and Vanessa will coordinate the SFTP endpoint details if you choose that route. If you want us to push an attested sample subset (7-day window) for your review we can schedule the job for Friday.

Sergio Alvarez
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
(attachment: admin_activity_export_spec.xlsx - spreadsheet, sftp_handshake_instructions.txt - text)

From: Anna Cole <anna.cole@optimalabs.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@optimalabs.com
Date: Wed, 16 May 2028 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity logging scope + export delivery preferences

Thanks, Sergio — that is very helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we schedule the sample export:

- For the attested snapshot, can you confirm the signing mechanism (do you use an internal cert? can you provide the public key/cert for verification?). We need to chain it to the signed manifest.
- For pseudonymization salt: will Optima Labs be able to provide a customer-specific salt so we can correlate exported hashes to our internal user IDs when needed?
- For SFTP: we will provide an endpoint and a deploy key. Can you confirm session user and chroot expectations (we prefer a single-directory chroot with a readonly user that Redwood writes into)?

If you can confirm those three items and then run the 7-day sample on Friday that would let our compliance team exercise the ingestion and manifest validation.

Best,
Anna

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Cole <anna.cole@optimalabs.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity logging scope + export delivery preferences

Anna — quick confirmations inline and next steps below.

1) Signing: we sign manifests with our evidence-signing key (RSA 4096) and include the signing cert. We will share the public cert PEM (chain) in the export bundle under certs/manifest_signer.pem; you can verify with standard OpenSSL tooling. We also include the signature as manifest.signature (base64) and the signing cert serial in manifest.signer_cert_id.

2) Customer salt: yes — we support a customer-provided salt for pseudonymization. On the request form please include the salt identifier and we will apply it deterministically to SHA256(username + salt). We log the salt_id used in the manifest so you can reconcile.

3) SFTP chroot/session: Redwood will open an SFTP session as "redwood-evidence" (UID-backed) and upload files into the directory you grant. We respect chrooted directories; our push will be simple PUTs (no recursive move). For atomicity we upload to a staging file name and then rename once complete. We require write + rename permissions. Please do not set mandatory server-side ACLs that block rename.

Action items we have taken now:
- Uploaded cert PEM (manifest_signer.pem) to the shared drive link: https://redwood-internal.share/ops/sftp-templates#evidence (see certs folder).
- Kim will reach out (kimberly.park@redwood.ai) to collect your SFTP host/key and schedule the Friday run (we prefer 10:00AM PT).
- Vanessa will prepare a terse attestation email template for your evidence packet.

If that all looks good I will queue a 7-day attested sample for Friday 10:00AM PT and email the manifest once complete.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
(attachment: export_sample_notice.txt - small delivery note)
